summary: Pomona sits in a spot that surprises people who only know it as a freeway name: the city backs up against the San Gabriel Mountains to the north, and on clear winter mornings — which are frequent given 9.3 hours of average daily sunshine — the snow-capped peaks loom startlingly close over a built-out valley floor. The presence of Cal Poly Pomona and Western University of Health Sciences gives the eastern half of the city a campus-and-research-park texture unusual for an Inland Valley community, and the Fairplex — home to the LA County Fair — occupies a 487-acre footprint that doubles as year-round event space, meaning Pomona functions partly as a regional job center rather than a pure bedroom community. That said, affordability math is tighter than it first appears: at a median income of roughly $79K and a median home value near $570K, the price-to-income ratio lands around 7.2, steep enough that buying requires well-above-median household earnings or substantial savings. Rent at $1,738 per month is more manageable but still claims over a quarter of that median gross income. The downtown strip along Second Street has accumulated a cluster of galleries and small restaurants — some tied to monthly art-walk events — giving the core a more intentional street-level identity than the surrounding auto-oriented commercial corridors. Motor vehicle theft runs notably high at 710 per 100K, a pattern consistent with the city's position along major freight and freeway corridors (the 10, 71, and 57 all converge here). Pomona is a city whose geography and institutional anchors punch above its price point, but whose infrastructure still reflects the fragmentation of being carved up by those same freeways.
